content.thinking:
I should clarify that the error rate stayed flat (-0.1%), so this was really a latency issue rather than an error spike, with a 6-minute duration and slow upstream io-pricing as the likely cause. The link between the restart and recovery is inferred from correlation rather than confirmed, so it could be coincidental, and I found no deploy or flag changes that would explain it.

I'm keeping the executive summary focused on qualitative details rather than restating the given cost/error figures as if I'd calculated them myself — I'll note things like the six-minute window and that errors didn't rise above baseline, but avoid asserting specific percentages as though they were my own computation.

assumptions: The link between the slow pricing dependency and io-shop's latency is a same-minute correlation plus matching log evidence, not a proven causal chain; no telemetry from inside io-pricing was examined to explain why it slowed down.

Recovery is attributed to the restart of io-pricing because the service was back at baseline ~22 seconds after it, but the fault was never reproduced and a spontaneous recovery coinciding with the restart cannot be ruled out.

'No change caused this' rests on a 137-minute lookback for deploys/releases and a check of recent feature-flag history; a change older than that window, or one made outside those systems, would not have been seen.
The ClientDisconnected errors in the logs were already present before onset and are read as shoppers abandoning slow or normal page loads, not as a distinct failure mode.
The alternative hypothesis - a change inside io-shop itself - was never tested, since the first candidate was confirmed and the incident closed.
Only 25 log lines over the 7 minutes before the alert were read, all from io-shop; the underlying trigger in the pricing service is therefore unknown and could recur.
input.executive_summary: For about six minutes shortly after midnight UTC on 26 September 2026 (00:12 to 00:18), the account page of the online shop was slow to load. Page loads still completed and the share of failed requests did not rise above its normal level, so the effect shoppers saw was waiting rather than errors. The cause was an internal service the shop calls to calculate basket totals, which started answering far more slowly than usual; every account page render had to wait for it. The automated responder picked up the alert at 00:17, traced the delay to that internal service within about fifteen seconds, and restarted it. The page returned to its normal response times by 00:18 and the incident was closed as mitigated. A draft code change intended to make the shop more resilient to a slow basket-total lookup was opened shortly afterwards for the owning team to review. Note that the alert fired several minutes after the slowdown began, so most of the affected window elapsed before anyone or anything was working the incident.
input.root_cause: An internal pricing dependency (io-pricing, pricing.io-internal.svc, owned by checkout-platform) began taking ~1500ms per call to /v1/shoppers/{id}/basket-total, and because io-shop makes that call synchronously while rendering the account page, the slow upstream saturated io-shop's request pools and drove p50/p95/p99 latency up roughly 30x from 00:12. No deploy, config, or feature-flag change was recorded on io-shop in the hours before onset, so the latency was propagated from the dependency rather than introduced locally.
